status: DRAFT. Rebuilt from the revised workbook, Fact Check and Source Register. practitioner_types and source_ids are derived from the steps in the workbook. Needs clinician approval.
age_notes: Ontario Living Concussion Guidelines linked here are adult-oriented. Steps use applies_to_ages and teen_note; teen content needs clinician approval.

categories.label: Fatigue/Activity
categories.mechanism_note: Energy-production explanations are not established by the cited sources. Do not state a mechanism to patients.
categories.typical_features: Ongoing physical or cognitive fatigue, brain fog, and symptoms that worsen after activity
categories.distinguishing_factors: Symptoms that worsen across thinking and physical tasks after minor effort. Edited from the original sheet wording; 'post-exertional malaise' removed unless a clinician uses it.
flags: Original sheet mechanism (mitochondrial ATP failure) cited a single case report and was removed per the audit.

categories.label: Exertional symptoms
categories.mechanism_note: A blood-flow (cerebrovascular) explanation is not established for individual patients by the cited sources. Do not state a mechanism to patients.
categories.typical_features: Headache, lightheadedness, or foggy thinking during or after physical activity
categories.distinguishing_factors: Symptoms appear within minutes of physical activity or a raised heart rate.
flags: Original sheet cited an acute-phase MRI study of 12 adults; it does not support a persistent-care pathway.

categories.label: Neuroendocrine
categories.mechanism_note: Testing is not routine for every concussion and depends on injury history and symptom pattern. Adult screening guidance only; teens need pediatric clinician input.
categories.typical_features: Fatigue, cold intolerance, unexplained weight shifts, and mood changes
categories.distinguishing_factors: Can resemble endocrine conditions such as hypothyroidism; only a clinician can tell, usually with blood tests. 'Adrenal fatigue' removed (not a recognized diagnosis).
flags: Symptoms are nonspecific. Do not imply they establish an endocrine problem.

categories.label: Vestibular
categories.typical_features: Dizziness in crowds and motion sickness
categories.distinguishing_factors: Provoked explicitly by visual motion or head turns.

categories.label: Oculomotor
categories.patient_label: Eye tracking, focusing and screen strain
categories.distinguishing_factors: Provoked explicitly by scrolling screens or tracking targets.
flags: Vision therapy evidence applies to diagnosed concussion-related convergence insufficiency, ages 11-25 (CONCUSS trial). Clinician to confirm which Canadian provider types deliver it; the trial used certified vision therapists.

categories.label: Sensory/Peripheral
categories.mechanism_note: Central sensitization and neck-driven light/noise sensitivity are not established by the cited sources. Do not state a mechanism to patients.
categories.typical_features: Daily tension headaches, neck stiffness, and sensitivity to light or noise
categories.distinguishing_factors: Localized tenderness in the upper neck muscles.
flags: Audit recommends splitting neck/vestibular symptoms from sensory sensitivity. Clinician to decide.
'Positive VOMS oculomotor triggers' was removed here because it overlaps with Vestibular and Oculomotor.
